messages:
liam: Heads-up — new sample app on Vercel Edge failing with our JS SDK. Error during import, looks like CJS/ESM mismatch. Anyone seen this?

maya: Ugh yeah, ran into something similar when testing the onboarding flow. Can you paste the error?

liam: Error from serverless logs: 
```
TypeError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
 at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:999:30)
 at Object.Module._extensions..js (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1027:10)
```
Seems like the function tried to exec ESM but file was CJS.

sasha: Are you bundling with esbuild/next? Vercel Edge expects ESM output. Check package.json exports and whether the edge entry points to an ESM build.

liam: It's the sample app in /examples/next-edge. package.json had "main": "dist/index.cjs.js" and "module": "dist/index.esm.js". Next's edge runtime pulled the CJS one for some reason.

julie: We should use conditional exports so ESM consumers (edge) get the ESM entry. Example: 
```json
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs"
}
```
And make sure the top-level "types" points to the universal d.ts (e.g. "./dist/index.d.ts").

maya: Also noticed TypeScript consumers are hitting weird typing errors after the change — generics + overloads break with our new signatures. Error like: 
```
TS2769: No overload matches this call.
```

sasha: That often happens when overloads rely on inference and you switch from any -> unknown in a refactor. Edge bundlers (esbuild) sometimes pick a different .d.ts via typesVersions mapping if present. Do you have typesVersions in package.json?

liam: Not currently. We tried to tighten types (replace any with unknown) to be safer but customers reported compile errors in older tsconfigs (ts 4.5/4.6).

julie: Two-pronged approach: 1) Fix packaging so edge imports ESM build. 2) Stabilize types with a compatibility surface. For overloads, prefer explicit generic constraints and a single generic entry point where possible. Example fix: 
```ts
// problematic
function createClient(options: CreateOptions): Client;
function createClient(authToken: string): Client;
// better
function createClient<T extends CreateOptions | string>(optsOrToken: T): Client;
```
If you must keep overloads, add an explicit cast helper for older TS.

maya: For unknown vs any: prefer unknown in public API but provide helper functions that accept any internally. Also adding a `lib` setting in tsconfig (esnext) helps inference in edge. Example tsconfig snippet that resolved a customer repro: 
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2020",
    "module": "ESNext",
    "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
    "types": ["node"],
    "skipLibCheck": true
  }
}
```

sasha: Another pattern is using typesVersions to point older TS/Node consumers to a .d.ts that uses looser types (uses any) while modern consumers get stricter definitions. Eg: 
```json
"typesVersions": {
  "<4.8": { "*": ["dist/types-compat/*"] },
  "*": { "*": ["dist/types/*"] }
}
```

liam: Good idea. Also the auth/retry stack uses Node's AbortController and global fetch polyfills — edge runtime has different signal semantics which caused hung retries. We got reports of requests that never aborted on Edge.

julie: We should guard runtime primitives. Example: 
```ts
const makeAbort = () => (typeof AbortController !== 'undefined' ? new AbortController() : polyfillAbortController());
```
And detect runtime via simple check so retry logic uses a compatible backoff.

maya: For onboarding friction, the sample app should detect runtime and choose the right bundle automatically. Maybe ship a tiny wrapper: 
```js
import { createClient as nodeCreate } from './node/index.cjs';
import { createClient as edgeCreate } from './edge/index.mjs';
export const createClient = typeof window === 'undefined' && typeof process !== 'undefined' ? nodeCreate : edgeCreate;
```
Not ideal but reduces surprise.

sasha: Long term, publish three artifacts: dist/node (CJS), dist/node-esm (for node ESM), dist/edge (pure ESM, edge-friendly). Use exports map with conditions: { "edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs", "import": "./dist/node-esm/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs" }.

sdk-bot: New issue created: #1234 - edge-sdk-packaging-and-typing-friction — assigned to @julie, @sasha. :white_check_mark:

liam: Action items from thread: 
- Julie: add conditional exports + types entry and publish canary.
- Sasha: prepare typesVersions + looser compat d.ts for older TS.
- Maya: update sample app to detect runtime and fallback.
- I'll add end-to-end test in the onboarding CI that deploys to Vercel Edge preview.

julie: I'll open a PR with the package.json changes + a small ci job to publish canary to npm.

maya: Happy to test the canary against the sample app.

sasha: One more note — document these patterns in the SDK contributor docs (packaging, types, edge caveats). People keep tripping over it. :memo:

liam: Agreed. Thanks all. :shipit:
